interest: This file provides valuable insight into how premier Japanese financial institutions navigated the outbreak and escalation of the Second Sino-Japanese War. It highlights the reliance of Japanese institutions like the Yokohama Specie Bank and the Bank of Chosen on neutral American nationals to safeguard their physical properties during the emergency evacuation of Tsingtao in August 1937. Furthermore, the 1939 telegram from Tientsin illustrates the complex jurisdictional landscape of foreign concessions in China, showing the Yokohama Specie Bank establishing a presence in the Japanese concession while prudently retaining its main office within the British concession.
overview: This file (decimal 894.51693) comprises State Department records from August 1937 to January 1939 regarding Japanese branch banks operating in China during the Second Sino-Japanese War. The file consists of two cross-reference sheets and one telegram documenting the activities and status of major Japanese financial institutions—specifically the Yokohama Specie Bank and the Bank of Chosen. In August 1937, following the outbreak of hostilities and the evacuation of Japanese nationals from Tsingtao (Qingdao), both banks entrusted their local properties to an American businessman. In January 1939, the American Consul General at Tientsin (Tianjin) reported that the Yokohama Specie Bank had opened a new branch in the Japanese concession while retaining its main office for the time being in the British concession.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a telegram from Tsingtao regarding the safeguarding of Japanese bank properties by an American businessman during the evacuation.
subfiles.summary: This State Department document file note cross-references an August 29, 1937 telegram (indexed under 793.94/9779) sent by Consul Samuel Sokobin from Tsingtao. It reports that amidst the Japanese evacuation of Tsingtao following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese conflict, the Yokohama Specie Bank and the Bank of Chosen requested a local American businessman to look after their property. The document was filed under decimal classification 894.51693 concerning Japanese branch banks in China.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Telegram from Tsingtao on Japanese Bank Property

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet citing a Navy Department communication concerning Japanese bank properties in Tsingtao.
subfiles.summary: This document file note cross-references an August 30, 1937 communication received from the Navy Department (filed under 793.94/9782). It corroborates reports that the Yokohama Specie Bank and the Bank of Chosen asked a local American businessman to safeguard their properties during the Japanese evacuation of Tsingtao. The note is indexed as 894.51693/6.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Navy Department Report on Japanese Banks in Tsingtao

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting that the Yokohama Specie Bank opened a branch in the Japanese concession in Tientsin while keeping its main office in the British concession.
subfiles.summary: Consul General John K. Caldwell telegraphs from Tientsin to the Secretary of State reporting local press news regarding the Yokohama Specie Bank. According to the press, the bank opened a new branch in the Japanese concession on January 5, 1939, while maintaining its main office in the British concession for the present. The telegram was copied to the U.S. Embassies in Chungking and Peiping, the Consulate General in Shanghai, and the Treasury Department.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Caldwell (Tientsin) on Yokohama Specie Bank Branch Opening
